guide:
# Ket: parametric CAD for agents

Ket is a parametric CAD and PCB tool that you drive with
tools. The design is a JSON document: parameters, an ordered list of named
features, and checks. Geometry is rebuilt from it by OpenCascade every time
it changes, so every dimension can be an expression over parameters.

## Coordinates
- Millimetres and degrees. Z is up. The XY plane at z=0 is the build plate.
- box is centered on X/Y and sits on z=0 by default; cylinder starts at the
  origin and grows along +axis.

## Projects and tabs
- Each open project is a tab in the user's Ket window; several can be open
  at once. Over MCP, open_project opens one (activate: false keeps the
  user's current tab), close_project closes it, and commands on a closed
  project open it in a background tab by themselves.

## Workflow
1. get_document to see what exists. If the project is new, set_description
   with the brief.
2. set_parameters for every dimension that matters (sizes, wall, clearances,
   hole positions). Derive the rest: case_w = "board_w + 2*wall + 2*gap".
3. set_checks for the requirements (fits, clearances, minimum walls) before
   modelling, so you can verify instead of guess.
4. Model with features, in a few calls: primitives and extrusions, then
   boolean (cut/union), then shell, then fillet/chamfer last.
5. run_checks after each group of changes. Fix every failed feature and
   failed check before continuing. Read warnings: a cut that removes nothing
   is a misplaced tool.
6. render (iso + another view) to look at the result when it matters, or
   section to see inside. Compare the picture with the intent.
7. Summarize for the user in a few lines.

## Sketches
- For any outline that is not a plain box or cylinder, sketch it: sketch
  on a plane, then extrude or revolve with sketch: "<name>".
- add_to_sketch shapes (rect, circle, slot, polygon) come fully
  constrained; loops inside the outer loop become holes.
- For custom outlines, give points (rough guesses are fine), lines/arcs that
  share points, and constraints (horizontal, vertical, length, distance,
  radius, tangent, ...). Drive values with parameters.
- solve_sketch after editing: aim for status "solved" with dof 0. A
  conflict names the constraint numbers to change.
- Revolve: draw the half cross-section on XZ on the +X side and revolve
  about Z.
- Loft blends between sections on parallel planes (rect base to round top);
  sweep moves a cross-section along a path of points with rounded corners
  (bend), for handles, channels and bent rods. Both need single loops: make
  hollow shapes by lofting/sweeping the inside too and cutting it.

## PCB
1. set_board with an outline (rect, or an XY sketch driven by the same
   parameters as the enclosure). The board becomes body "board" and each
   part "part_<REF>" in the 3D model.
2. find_parts by part number, part_info to see pins, add_component by LCSC
   number. Prefer JLCPCB basic parts in stock.
3. connect pins into nets by name ("U1.VIN", "J1.GND"); set_net_class for
   power nets (e.g. 0.5 mm).
4. Place parts with room to route: connectors at the edge, decoupling caps
   next to their pins. get_board shows sizes; run_drc catches overlaps.
5. autoroute, then run_drc. Fix violations, re-route if needed.
6. render_board to look at it; export_fab writes the JLCPCB package.
7. For an enclosure: model around "board" / "part_*" bodies and verify with
   checks (inside, no_overlap, min_distance).

## Rules of thumb
- Name features by purpose: case_body, usb_cutout, standoff_pattern.
- A feature's inputs are consumed: after a cut only the result is a body.
- To change a feature, use update_feature (a few fields) or the feature
  command with replace: true; everything downstream rebuilds.
- Selectors pick faces/edges by meaning (">Z" top, "|Z" vertical edges).
  Check them with list_faces / list_edges when unsure.
- Make cutting tools overlap the material they cut by at least 0.5 mm on
  each open side, and avoid coplanar faces between tool and target.
- Prefer one shell over many cuts for enclosures; add clearance (0.2-0.5 mm)
  for parts that must fit together when 3D printed.
- If a command fails, read the message: it says what to change.

commands.name: set_parameters
commands.description: Create or update named parameters. Values are numbers (mm, degrees) or expressions over other parameters. Use parameters for every dimension that matters (board size, wall, clearance) so the design stays editable: change one and every feature that uses it rebuilds.

expr.description: Number in mm (or degrees), or an expression over parameters such as "wall*2 + 0.2"

commands.name: delete_parameters
commands.description: Delete parameters. Fails while a parameter, feature or check still uses one of them.

commands.name: box
commands.description: Add a box. By default it is centered on X and Y and sits on Z=0 (from z=0 to z=size[2]). Set center to choose per axis: [true,true,false] is the default, true centers all axes, false puts the corner at the origin.

commands.name: extrude
commands.description: Extrude a closed 2D outline into a solid. Either sketch (a constrained sketch, see the sketch command; holes inside the outline stay holes) or a quick profile on a plane (rect with optional corner r, circle, slot, polygon). XY extrudes along +Z from z=offset, XZ along +Y, YZ along +X; a negative distance goes the other way; symmetric centers it on the sketch plane.

commands.name: loft
commands.description: Blend a solid through 2 or more cross-sections in order (e.g. a rectangle at the base to a circle at the top: funnels, transitions, tapered bosses). Each section is a sketch or a profile on a plane with an offset; sections are usually parallel and spaced along the normal. Each must be one closed loop without holes (cut holes afterwards). ruled: straight faces between sections instead of a smooth blend.

commands.name: sweep
commands.description: Sweep a cross-section along a 3D path (cable channels, handles, bent rods, gaskets). The path goes straight through the points; bend rounds every corner with that radius (recommended, sharp corners are mitered). The cross-section (profile or sketch, in its own u/v coordinates) is centered on the first point, perpendicular to the first segment; u is horizontal (perpendicular to the path and Z) and v is up. One loop without holes: for a tube sweep the inner profile too and cut it.

commands.name: set_appearance

commands.name: rename_feature

commands.name: delete_features

commands.name: set_checks
commands.description: Add or replace (by name) design checks: requirements that run_checks verifies after every change. Write the requirements first, then model, then run_checks. Kinds: expr (boolean over parameters), min_distance (clearance between two bodies), no_overlap, inside (inner fits in outer with margin), volume (min/max).

outer.description: Usually a body representing the free space, e.g. the cavity of a case

margin.description: Minimum gap to every side of the outer bounding box

min.description: Number in mm (or degrees), or an expression over parameters such as "wall*2 + 0.2"

items.description: A requirement the design must keep meeting

commands.name: delete_checks
commands.description: Delete design checks by name.

commands.name: set_description
commands.description: Set the design brief: what is being built and the key requirements, in a few lines. It is shown to every agent that opens the project.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Apply several changes atomically as one step (one undo): if any step fails, nothing changes and the error names the step. Use it to build a whole part in one call. Steps are change commands only (no queries).

args.description: Its arguments, as when calling it directly

commands.name: sketch
commands.description: Create (or with replace: true redefine) a constrained 2D sketch on a plane. Plane coordinates (u, v): XY → (x, y) at z = offset, XZ → (x, z) at y = offset, YZ → (y, z) at x = offset. Points are starting guesses; constraints hold the intent and the solver moves the points. Lines and arcs that share points form closed outlines; loops inside loops become holes. Use parameters in values so the sketch follows the design. Shortcuts: add_to_sketch with rect/circle/slot/polygon. Then extrude or revolve it with sketch: "<name>".

plane.description: Sketch plane: XY extrudes along +Z, XZ along +Y, YZ along +X

offset.description: Number in mm (or degrees), or an expression over parameters such as "wall*2 + 0.2"

x.description: Number in mm (or degrees), or an expression over parameters such as "wall*2 + 0.2"

y.description: Number in mm (or degrees), or an expression over parameters such as "wall*2 + 0.2"

fixed.description: The solver will not move it

end.description: The arc runs counter-clockwise from start to end

commands.name: remove_from_sketch
commands.description: Remove points, entities or constraints from a sketch. Constraints are referenced by their 1-based number as solve_sketch lists them. Removing a point also removes the entities and constraints using it.

commands.name: delete_sketch
commands.description: Delete a sketch. Fails while a feature uses it.

commands.name: solve_sketch
commands.description: Solve a sketch and report: status (solved / conflict / redundant / failed), degrees of freedom left (0 = fully constrained; aim for 0 so parameter changes behave), conflicting or redundant constraints by number, solved point positions, and the closed loops found (what extrude/revolve will use).

commands.name: set_board
commands.description: Create or change the PCB: outline (a rect, or an XY sketch whose inner loops become cut-outs), thickness, copper layers (2 or 4) and z (height of the board's bottom face, so an enclosure can be modelled around it). The board appears in the 3D model as body "board" and each part as "part_<REF>" (a block of its courtyard and height): use them in checks and booleans (e.g. inside part_J1 the case cavity, or a cut where J1 meets the wall).

commands.name: find_parts
commands.description: Search the LCSC / JLCPCB parts library. The search matches part numbers and manufacturers best ("AMS1117-3.3", "TYPE-C-31-M-12", "0603WAF1002T5E"), not descriptions. Prefer basic parts (cheaper assembly) and parts in stock. Returns LCSC numbers for add_component.

commands.name: part_info
commands.description: Show an LCSC part before adding it: manufacturer part number, package, stock, and its pins (pad number → name) and pad positions.

commands.name: add_component
commands.description: Place a real part from LCSC on the board by its LCSC number (from find_parts). ref is chosen automatically (U1, R3, ...) unless given. at is the part center in board coordinates [x, y] (expressions allowed), rotation in degrees CCW, side top or bottom. value is the BOM comment ("10k", "100nF").

commands.name: remove_components
commands.description: Remove parts; their pins leave every net.

commands.name: connect
commands.description: Connect pins into named nets. Pins are REF.PIN with the pad number or the pin name from the part ("U1.3", "U1.VIN", "J1.GND"; a name on several pads takes all of them). Existing nets with the same name are extended. A pin already on another net is moved to this one. Connect everything before placing and routing.

commands.name: disconnect
commands.description: Remove pins from their nets, or delete whole nets by name.

commands.name: wire_pins
commands.description: Wire pins together, as drawing a wire on the schematic does. Pins on no net form a new net (named net, or N1, N2…); a pin joins the net of the others; pins on different nets merge them into one (the given name, else the first name that is not an automatic N…), and the copper of merged nets follows. Prefer connect when you know the net names.

pins.description: REF.PIN, e.g. ["U1.VOUT", "C2.1"]; drawn as a chain of wires

points.description: Bend points of the wire (two pins only), schematic units

commands.name: remove_wires
commands.description: Remove schematic wires (each given by its two pins, in any order). On an automatic net (N1, N2…) this also cuts the connection: the pins split into the groups the remaining wires join, and a pin left alone leaves the net. On a named net only the drawing goes; use disconnect to cut it.

commands.name: rename_net
commands.description: Rename a net (and its tracks, vias and pours). Renaming onto an existing net merges the two.

commands.name: set_net_class
commands.description: Create or change a net class: track width, clearance and via size for its nets (e.g. "power": 0.5 mm tracks). The "default" class applies to every other net.

commands.name: add_track
commands.description: Draw a track by hand: a polyline on one copper layer for a net. Width defaults to the net class. Usually autoroute does this; use add_track for short fixes.

commands.name: add_via
commands.description: Add a via for a net at [x, y]; size defaults to the net class.

commands.name: unroute
commands.description: Remove tracks and vias: of the listed nets, or all of them.

commands.name: add_zone
commands.description: Add a copper pour for a net on a layer, usually GND on B.Cu (and/or F.Cu). Without polygon it covers the whole board. The fill keeps clearance to other nets, ties same-net pads with thermal spokes and drops islands that reach no pad of the net. Add pours after placing parts; autoroute routes the other nets and leaves the pour net to the pour, so add GND vias next to F.Cu GND pads when pouring only on B.Cu.

polygon.description: Board coordinates; default the whole board

clearance.description: To other nets; default the net class clearance

commands.name: remove_zones
commands.description: Remove copper pours by number (1-based, as get_board lists them), or all of a net.

commands.name: add_mounting_hole
commands.description: Add non-plated mounting holes (e.g. d 2.7 for M2.5 screws). Use the same parameters as the enclosure standoffs so they line up.

prefixItems.description: Number in mm (or degrees), or an expression over parameters such as "wall*2 + 0.2"
Number in mm (or degrees), or an expression over parameters such as "wall*2 + 0.2"

commands.name: autoroute
commands.description: Route the board with Freerouting (on the server): every net with 2+ pins, keeping existing tracks. Takes seconds to a few minutes. Place parts and set net classes first; then run_drc. If nets stay unrouted, give parts more room or allow 4 layers.

commands.name: get_board
commands.description: Read the board: outline size, parts (ref, part, package, position, rotation, side, size), nets with their pins (and pin names), routing status (which nets are still unrouted, with the missing connections) and copper counts.

commands.name: run_drc
commands.description: Design rule check against JLCPCB's standard capabilities: parts inside the outline and not overlapping, track width, clearance and shorts between nets, copper to edge, drills and hole spacing, plus unrouted nets. Each violation names the objects and the measured value.

commands.name: render_board
commands.description: Draw the board from above (or below): outline, pads, tracks (top red, bottom blue), vias, refs, ratsnest lines for missing connections and red markers at DRC violations. highlight draws parts or nets in orange.

commands.name: export_fab
commands.description: Write the JLCPCB fabrication package as a zip download: Gerber X2 for copper, mask, silk and outline, Excellon drill, BOM and CPL for assembly. Refuses while DRC fails or nets are unrouted unless force is true.

commands.name: check_bom
commands.description: Check the bill of materials for an order of boards: per part the quantity, LCSC stock, unit price and line cost (rounded up to LCSC minimum/step), JLCPCB basic or extended (extended parts add a $3 setup fee each), and problems: out of stock, not enough stock for the order, parts without an LCSC number. Prices are refreshed when older than a day. Use it before export_fab, and to pick cheaper or basic alternatives (find_parts).

boards.description: Number of boards to build, default 5

commands.name: render_schematic
commands.description: Draw the schematic: every part's symbol with its pin names, wires where they were drawn (wire_pins) and a net label on connected pins a wire does not fully show (pins with the same label are connected). It is generated from the netlist, so it always matches the board. Use it to review the circuit: unconnected pins have no wire and no label.

commands.name: place_symbol
commands.description: Move symbols on the schematic (grid units of 10 mil; the auto layout is used for parts without a position). Purely visual: nets do not change.

at.description: Omit to return to auto layout

commands.name: get_document
commands.description: Read the design: parameters (with resolved values), features in order with their inputs, bounding boxes, volumes, errors and warnings, the checks and the visible bodies. Start every task with it. detail "full" includes every field of every feature.

commands.name: get_feature

commands.name: measure
commands.description: Measure a feature: bounding box, size, volume, surface area, center of mass. With other: also the minimum distance between the two and the volume they overlap (0 = no collision).

commands.name: measure_between
commands.description: Distance between two things, each a feature (body, part_<REF>, board) or a point [x, y, z]. Two features: the minimum gap and their overlap volume; point and feature: the gap from the point to the surface (0 when inside); two points: the distance and the vector between them. Use it for clearances, e.g. a connector to the case wall.

a.description: A feature name or a point [x, y, z] in mm

b.description: A feature name or a point [x, y, z] in mm

commands.name: run_checks
commands.description: Rebuild and verify the design: every feature must build, and every check (set_checks) must pass. Run it after each group of changes and fix what fails before going on.

commands.name: render
commands.description: Render the model to images to see it. Default views: iso and top. Front looks along +Y (from -Y), right looks along -X, top looks down -Z. highlight draws the named features in orange; hide leaves features out (e.g. a lid); section cuts the view at a plane to look inside. Images come with a short text legend.

section.description: Remove everything on the positive side of the plane

at.description: Coordinate of the cut plane in mm

commands.name: export
commands.description: Export bodies as STEP (CAD exchange) or STL (3D printing). The file is downloaded in the user's browser. Default: all visible bodies. Board parts export as their part_* blocks (courtyard × real model height); with detail: "models" STEP gets the vendor 3D models instead (meshes sewn into faces: true shapes for checking fit in another CAD tool, but larger files, about 20 MB per detailed part). To print an enclosure alone, pass names: ["case"].

detail.description: Board parts as blocks (default) or as vendor models (STEP)
